finding.claim: With caching enabled, verify() throws a TypeError instead of a TokenError when given a Buffer token, because the default cacheKeyBuilder (hashToken) calls String.prototype.split on the Buffer before decoding.
finding.source: Caller-supplied token of type Buffer (accepted by the type guard at src/verifier.js:361).
finding.sink: hashToken token.split('.', 1) at src/utils.js:46, invoked from src/verifier.js:372 before decode.

trace.note: Buffer tokens pass the type guard.
Cache branch runs only when cache is enabled.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) is called on the raw token, before the try around decode at line 392.
token.split is not a function on a Buffer, so a TypeError is thrown.

finding.guards_checked: Type guard at verifier.js:361 accepts Buffers. The decode try/catch at verifier.js:392-401 is after the cache lookup and does not cover it. The cache is only created when the cache option is set (createCache, verifier.js:94-97; default is no cache, since parseInt(undefined) is NaN). No guard converts the Buffer to a string before hashToken. Impact is limited: an exception escapes verify() instead of a rejection or callback error, and only when the caller enables cache and passes Buffers. No authentication bypass.
